newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after ECI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after ECI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Tuesday after a report on the second quarter Employment Cost Index (ECI) matched expectations, analysts said. The following are their comments:

PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT: "It's all clean and as expected. It's right in line (and) there does not appear to be any surprises. We remain in an environment of moderate growth and benign inflation."
The U.S. Labor Department reported the second quarter ECI rose 0.8 percent, matching economists' consensus expectation.

ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST AT FAHNESTOCK AND CO: The ECI data was "one of the numbers that was of real concern to Fed watchers. All in all, it's not a bad number and momentum is likely to be stimulated by reaction to the budget deal, which it appears is going to steal the thunder from the data today."

HILDEGARD ZAGORSKI, AN ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES: "The ECI was right in line and bonds are up a small fraction. It was a good number. We'll probably have a firmer open and a fairly decent day. I don't see anything to stand in the market's way."
The 30-year Treasury bond, after initially moving higher in reaction to the data, was off 4/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
The S&P 500 future, also slipped after first moving higher. It was off 1.50 to 942.15.
